**SHOCKER IN COLLEGE HOOPS: Indonesian Football Star Wismoyo Widhistio Trades Cleats for Sneakers, Joins The Citadel Bulldogs Basketball**

Charleston, SC - In a stunning move that has left fans and pundits alike scratching their heads, Indonesian football sensation Wismoyo Widhistio has announced his decision to trade in his cleats for sneakers, joining the men's college basketball team at The Citadel Bulldogs. The 25-year-old Widhistio, who has made a name for himself on the international football stage with his lightning-quick speed and razor-sharp agility, revealed his surprising career shift in an exclusive interview with our publication. "I've always had a passion for basketball, and I felt it was time to challenge myself in a new way," Widhistio said, donning a Citadel Bulldogs jersey and flashing a bright smile. "The Citadel's rich history and commitment to excellence resonated with me, and I'm excited to bring my unique skillset to the court." Widhistio's decision has sent shockwaves through the college basketball community, with many wondering how a footballer with no prior basketball experience could make the transition to the hardwood. However, Citadel Bulldogs head coach Duggar Baucom is confident that Widhistio's athleticism and work ethic will translate seamlessly to the court. "Wismoyo is an incredible athlete, and we're thrilled to have him on board," Baucom said. "He's already shown a remarkable aptitude for the game, and we're excited to see him develop his skills further. His speed and agility will undoubtedly create matchup nightmares for our opponents." According to sources close to the team, Widhistio has been working tirelessly in the offseason to adapt to the nuances of basketball, putting in extra hours in the gym to hone his shooting and ball-handling skills. The Citadel Bulldogs, who finished last season with a 12-18 record, are looking to bounce back with a strong campaign this year. With Widhistio's addition, the team is hoping to capitalize on his international fame and attract a new wave of fans to McAlister Field House. "Wismoyo's presence will undoubtedly bring a level of excitement and energy to our program," said Citadel athletic director Mike Capaccio. "We're looking forward to seeing him make an impact on the court and in the community."
